question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The system corresponding to $M$ is 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2y &=1 \\ 0x+0y &=0.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x-2y=1.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=1+2y,$ and the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=1+2y \\ y &=y\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}1+2y \\ y\end{bmatrix}=⟨1+2y,\,y⟩,\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}4 & -16 & 8 \\ -3 & 12 & -6\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}4 & -16 & 8 \\ -3 & 12 & -6\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -4 & 2 \\ -3 & 12 & -6\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}3 & -9 & 6 \\ 4 & -12 & 8\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}3 & -9 & 6 \\ 4 & -12 & 8\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -3 & 2 \\ 4 & -12 & 8\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 4 & -2 \\ -5 & -10 & 5\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}2 & 4 & -2 \\ -5 & -10 & 5\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & -1 \\ -5 & -10 & 5\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+5{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$
